entities.summary:
Gerolamo Emiliani, CRS, was an Italian humanitarian and founder of the Somaschi Fathers, considered a saint by the Catholic Church.

Born in Modena, Italy, around 1500, Emiliani dedicated his life to caring for the poor and sick, marking a commitment to social justice and the empowerment of marginalized communities.

Following his death in 1537, Emiliani's legacy continued to inspire Catholic reform and humanitarian efforts, shaping the Somaschi Order into a prominent force for social welfare and education.

In recognition of his tireless service, the Catholic Church beatified Emiliani in 1692, paving the way for his eventual canonization in 1769.

As the founder of the Somaschi Fathers, Emiliani's work remains a testament to the enduring power of compassion and commitment to the common good.

Gerolamo Emiliani's remarkable life serves as a powerful reminder of the transformative impact one individual can have on the world, inspiring generations of social reformers and humanitarian activists.

The Somaschi Order, founded by Emiliani, continues to operate in Italy and around the world, upholding the values of empathy, solidarity, and service that defined its founder's life's work.
